visualLanguage.name: Editorial Correspondence
principles: Use editorial rhythm, alignment, and hairline rules before containers or decoration.
Keep resting surfaces borderless; rules separate dense rows and state rings communicate focus or error.
Use near-square two-pixel corners. Circles are reserved for identity, presence, and unread state.
Keep layouts compact while preserving a minimum 44pt iOS and 48dp Android touch target.
Reserve color for interaction and semantic state; ordinary hierarchy stays neutral.

typography.display: Source Serif 4 at display optical sizes for Latin/Greek/Cyrillic and Source Han Serif CN Semibold for Chinese introductions and major headings; Japanese and Korean use locale-correct native serif faces.
typography.reading: Source Serif 4 at text optical sizes for Latin/Greek/Cyrillic and Source Han Serif CN Regular/Semibold for Chinese messages, previews, and long-form copy; Japanese and Korean use locale-correct native serif faces.
typography.utility: Source Sans 3 on Web and the native platform sans on iOS/Android for entity names, navigation labels, controls, trace, metadata, warning, and status. The native sans fallback remains locale-correct for CJK and other scripts. Monospace is a technical sub-role for code only.

shape.separator: hairline rules for editorial or dense scanning surfaces

icons.productSemantics: Cheers editorial icon register on a 24-unit grid with a 1.75-unit stroke.
icons.utilityActions: Use the closest platform-native or established library icon.
icons.rule: Prefer one distinct silhouette per product concept; do not vary one document glyph for unrelated meanings.

max.description: Full identity, primary and secondary content, preview, critical state, and common actions.

medium.description: Identity, title, one supporting line, critical state, and a primary or overflow action.

minimal.description: Minimum identity and title while preserving critical state. Non-critical actions move to an owning menu.

comfortable.description: Primary navigation, workspace rail, and prominent touch controls.

regular.description: Default buttons, fields, list items, and composer controls.

compact.description: Dense desktop utilities and section controls; touch viewports retain a 44px hit target.

invariants: An explicit item presentation level overrides the inherited container level.
Responsive rules may choose an inherited default but never replace an explicit item level.
Critical error, approval, unread, mention, and online state remains perceivable at every level.
Presentation level changes information density, not business behavior or API data.
Control size changes physical height, not visible information or business state.
Presentation level and control size inherit and override independently.
Web, iOS, and Android share anatomy and semantics while retaining platform-native navigation, motion, typography, and accessibility behavior.
